title: Chapter 1127
paragraphs: Chapter 1127
Episode 258. The Predator of All Dimensions (17)

Touven was dead, and Murakan was delirious and couldn't fight properly. Moreover, since the red sea was continuously driving the Coalition members mad, the tide of the central front was completely turning to the Demon Army.
Explosions and screams.
A crimson sea and fire, and over them, pouring blood and ash.
He had no choice but to turn his back on his dying comrades. Jin had no choice but to wander through Kelliark's desire, leaning on the faint word Orgal had spoken: hope.
Every step was agony.

Every time he stepped on the red seawater, it felt like a thousand hooks were piercing his entire body. It felt like they were screaming at him to collapse, to sink into this place and stop. Jin's eyes wavered blankly, then hardened, over and over again.
"Sister Luna."
"Jin."
"We must protect Lafrarosa."
If they simply left the central front as it was, Lafrarosa would inevitably be in danger too.

Jin chose Luna as the card to support them. Orgal could barely stand, and Chiron and Vahn needed to protect him from Kelliark until the very end. There was no guarantee that Heluram would definitely hold out for an hour.
"Alright, I'll go."
Luna nodded, answering in a hoarse voice.
"Don't die."

"I would rather die myself. Isn't it the same for you? It's much better than not being able to protect them. At nineteen... I decided to become the sword that guards the family. I will survive to the end and save even one more person, somehow."
Gurgle, gurgle...!
The red sea was churning. Soon, from the moment Luna started running towards the back of the battlefield, a scene followed where darkness descended upon it.
Heluram had begun to use her last remaining authority.
"Jin, where will you go?"
"...I don't know, Father."
Where should he go?

Where in this red sea and darkness was the entrance to Solderet's sanctuary hidden? Where was the future they had been pursuing? He didn't know. With Valeria unconscious, he couldn't even track a small clue.
"So I must just move forward. Father, Sister Vahn. Please open a path. In any direction..."
"I will."
Compared to the red energy spreading from the sea and the abyss covering the sky, the swords of the two Genesis Knights shone faintly and dimly, like candlelight.
"Follow well, even if it's hard."
"Yes, Father."
Jin tore his coat and tied Valeria more tightly to his body. Fortunately, Enya was conscious enough to hold Jin's hand and run.
[Hey Jin... can't you do something for me too? Hold me, I can't walk.]
"Take my hand, Orgal."
[Dammit, I wanted to be comfortable at the end.]
Valeria tied to Jin, Enya holding his hand, and Orgal holding her hand.
For a moment, Jin let out a chuckle at their ridiculous appearance. And he was thankful that he still had the strength to laugh.

Looking back, from Kinzelo onwards, most of the beings called gods had not been very beneficial to people. In the first place, Jin had never fervently believed in or followed even Solderet, so it wasn't that he felt a sense of gratitude towards a divine being.
For some reason, he just felt thankful to the world. Even if it was this desperate, even if it was so sad that he could hardly bear it, for some reason, he felt he should.
"Kahaaaa!"
Chiron's roar, which would normally have shaken the entire battlefield, sank into the desire and darkness and became an empty cry.

As if responding to his voice, the sea of desire was raging fiercely. Like a ship caught in a storm, the Genesis Knights had to endure Kelliark's desire pouring into their mouths, ears, and noses from the very beginning.
But Jin, Valeria, Enya, and Orgal were not covered in the red seawater. It was thanks to Chiron and Vahn desperately protecting them.
"Haaa...!"

How were Kelliark and Heluram fighting? The Genesis Knights didn't even have the leisure to look at them. If they looked back for even a moment, they would be swept away and disappear somewhere into the raging waves.

The sound of the viscous, blood-like seawater churning was just making them dizzy. They spat, vomited, and swung their swords, and the view ahead would be momentarily submerged in darkness, then stained red.
He couldn't gauge how many steps he had taken, or in what direction he was going at all. The ever-rising waves now seemed poised to cover even the shockwaves spreading from the central front.
[Luck... looking back, you've always been lucky, Jin.]
"That's right, Young Master Jin has always been followed by great luck."

Chiron and Vahn, of course, had no leisure to speak, and Jin had no capacity either, busy protecting the people attached to him. He had to grit his teeth to ward off the water that was breaking through Chiron and Vahn's sword-curtain.
Therefore, only Enya and Orgal could speak. Of course, they too were trembling from Kelliark's desire stirring in their minds.

They should have been pouring all their mental energy into overcoming the desire, but for some reason, they felt they had to speak. Because if not now, they might never be able to talk to these people again; because if not them, no one could shout encouragement to them.
[It was painful when we were enemies. What the hell is this bastard, why does everything always go so well for him... We were always used like fools. But now I think I know the reason.]
"Is there a reason for luck?"
[There is. From what I see, this world loves that bastard. And it hates that bastard Kelliark very much. By the way, is Heluram holding up well, ku-hak.]

Enya didn't tell Orgal, who was suddenly coughing up a clot of blood, to stop talking. Instead, she removed the heavy clot of blood from his chest with her hand and scrubbed his mouth with her sleeve. As if he were a person who could live an hour later, and tomorrow.
[Ugh, your hand smells terrible.]
"I've been fighting for five days without a wink of sleep, so of course it does. So you don't like it?"

[No. It's a stench I don't think I'll ever forget, even if I become a soldier of the abyss again. So it's even better. I'll be a soldier who remembers one more thing besides my grudge against Kelliark.]

The longer they walked, the shorter the interval between Orgal spitting out clots of blood became. At times, he would even cough up small fragments that looked like bone. Each time, Enya silently wiped his mouth.
[...Anyway, what I wanted to say is, you can find it. Jin, you can find it. But what were we... looking for right now?]
"Solderet's sanctuary, isn't it?"
[Right, that. It's probably waiting for you in a whole state. So, uh, you can find it.]
The limit of Orgal's life was approaching. He could no longer even walk straight and was at the point of being barely dragged along by Enya.
The more Orgal rambled, the tighter Enya held his hand.
Chiron and Vahn swinging their swords like demons to part the red sea for even a moment, Jin lowering his head and momentarily stopping his movements every two seconds.
In the midst of that, talking alone for them was more frightening than death, more frightening than being buried in Kelliark's desire.
"Young Master Jin, it seems Heluram is still fighting well. The sea is in an uproar, but still, Kelliark hasn't attacked this side directly yet. Don't you think so too, Orgal?"
[Uh... huh? What?]
"Just say yes."
The moment Orgal was about to answer, Jin spoke for the first time.
"...Valeria."
"Young Master Jin?"
"Valeria isn't breathing."
Enya moved closer to Jin and checked Valeria's pulse. Then she covered her mouth and swallowed a sob. The pulse was not beating at all, and her body was just cold like a shadow.
Jin did not stop walking. He couldn't feel the sorrow. It was just that he couldn't stop walking to shake off the vague sense of loss.
[Dammit...]
Orgal spoke a beat later.
He wasn't talking about Valeria's breath stopping. The reason he spoke now was that he had felt sun energy.
Hwaaaa...
Suddenly, the darkness was lifting. The battlefield was brightening as if dawn had suddenly arrived. A vast light spreading from somewhere was seen shattering over the red sea.
[He's... resurrecting. Through Kelliark, the Sun God.]
Chiron and Vahn looked back for the first time.
There, stood Kelliark with his back to the sun. He had stolen the power of Malugia and Araxion while dealing with Heluram, and now the result of that was beginning to appear on the battlefield.
Heluram was collapsed in front of him, gasping for breath. She was struggling to get up, not like an immortal, but like a tired and injured ordinary human.
"Ah, the being who created this world is such a simply constructed being... if you just gather the pieces, was it this easy to put them together?"
Kelliark said, looking down at Heluram.

Although Heluram hadn't been completely annihilated yet, it seemed she no longer had the strength to stop Kelliark. Her body was slowly disintegrating just by being exposed to the light radiating from Kelliark.
Still, it wasn't that Heluram hadn't dealt him any damage. Kelliark touched the area around his eyes with his hand and shrugged.
"You couldn't defeat me, so you blind me even for a moment. That must have been the best you could do."
Kinzelo's power was not yet perfectly bound to Kelliark. Just as the Origin Stone needed time to be purified, it was the same for him.

Therefore, Kelliark couldn't immediately shake off Heluram's darkness that had blinded him. But even if he couldn't see, attacking the enemies was an easy task. He just had to indiscriminately fire sun energy all over, make the red sea rage even stronger, and cause a disaster.
"It is truly a pity that I cannot see your final moments in person, Jin Runcandel. But I don't want to be complacent."
Kelliark raised his hand. Then, streaks of light began to pour from the sky. Streaks of light that passed through the Genesis Knights' swords and Lafrarosa's shield as if they were all illusions.
There was only one place to hide. The red sea. They had to throw themselves into it to block that light.
Jin raised his head and looked at a single streak of light falling towards his face.
He couldn't block it.
It was a light that fell faster than the blink of an eye. Death. If the light pierced his head like this, death would surely come.
But at that moment.
The falling light stopped. Jin, his gaze fixed on the sharp light that had stopped before his eyes, thought about what had happened.
'Time... has it stopped?'
Time had stopped.
And Jin could see a blue window filling his view, blocking the light.
It was Valeria's recording window.
